abstract_sentences.text: We present Depth Anything 3 (DA3), a model that predicts spatially consistent geometry from an arbitrary number of visual inputs, with or without known camera poses.

evidence.anchor: arbitrary number of visual inputs, with or without known camera poses

abstract_sentences.text: In pursuit of minimal modeling, DA3 yields two key insights: a single plain transformer (e.g., vanilla DINO encoder) is sufficient as a backbone without architectural specialization, and a singular depth-ray prediction target obviates the need for complex multi-task learning.

evidence.anchor: a single plain transformer; a singular depth-ray prediction target

abstract_sentences.text: Through our teacher-student training paradigm, the model achieves a level of detail and generalization on par with Depth Anything 2 (DA2).

evidence.anchor: teacher-student training paradigm; on par with Depth Anything 2

abstract_sentences.text: We establish a new visual geometry benchmark covering camera pose estimation, any-view geometry and visual rendering.

evidence.anchor: new visual geometry benchmark covering camera pose estimation, any-view geometry and visual rendering

abstract_sentences.text: On this benchmark, DA3 sets a new state-of-the-art across all tasks, surpassing prior SOTA VGGT by an average of 35.7% in camera pose accuracy and 23.6% in geometric accuracy.

evidence.anchor: 35.7% in camera pose accuracy and 23.6% in geometric accuracy

abstract_sentences.text: Moreover, it outperforms DA2 in monocular depth estimation.

evidence.anchor: outperforms DA2 in monocular depth estimation

abstract_sentences.text: All models are trained exclusively on public academic datasets.

evidence.anchor: trained exclusively on public academic datasets

claim_closure.claim: Depth-ray is a minimal sufficient target set.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Recover a consistent visual space from arbitrary views using depth plus per-pixel rays, a pretrained single transformer and adaptive cross-view attention; teacher–student labels handle mixed data, a camera head accelerates pose extraction, and GS-DPT transfers the backbone to FF-NVS.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the ray projection, architecture components, teacher rationale, benchmark definitions, Tables 1–6 and the primary pose/geometry/monocular/NVS decisions.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: DLT/RQ extraction, loss details, teacher normal/mask targets, sampling/alignment, dataset thresholds, training budgets, baseline descriptions, scale/speed and extended ablations move to pages 17–25.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A single teaser visual contract plus a benchmark-aligned sequence of main tables, followed by target-level and architecture-level ablations, makes the minimal-representation claim easy to audit.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Point estimates have no uncertainty; geometry-to-NVS “correlation” has no association statistic; teacher and pose-conditioning ablations mix conditions; ScanNet++ and GT-pose caveats are distributed rather than centrally resolved.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a unified representation claim, show the input–representation–output chain first, then one target ablation and one architecture ablation; move reproducibility-critical sampling, alignment, loss and budget details to a locatable appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits visual/system papers with an explicit intermediate representation and controlled component substitutions; pure-theory or single-task papers need theorem-to-corollary or mechanism-to-prediction closure instead.
